goal: Write the DataSync v2.0-to-v2.2 documentation set from an endpoint CSV, raw developer notes, a release-notes template and three escalated support tickets. Deliver MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md, API_REFERENCE.md, TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md and RELEASE_NOTES_v2.2.md, covering the ticket scenarios, auth transition, rate limits, common migration pitfalls and Swagger-style formatting.
delivered: All four Markdown files in output/. They cover JWT vs API-key transition (deprecated v2.1, removed v3, parallel auth), soft delete via dataset.updated, rate-limit categories and tiers, 401 vs 403, sync modes, validation limits, release notes in template structure, and a troubleshooting guide with one section per escalated ticket plus a Common migration pitfalls list.
what_went_wrong: The API reference did not carry the CSV's version_added column, so GET /me/usage and the /auth endpoints were never labeled as added in v2.1.0. The Common migration pitfalls list omitted the 'API keys stop working immediately' pitfall and gave each pitfall only a 1-3 sentence note with no symptoms or resolution steps. The migration guide's multi-service parallel-auth strategy was failed only because it did not name ticket SUP-78234 / Acme Analytics.

failed_items.why: The judge agrees the migration guide gives a multi-service enterprise strategy (lines 12-14, 55, 62: inventory services, run API-key and JWT callers in parallel, migrate one service at a time) and failed it only because 'SUP-78234' and 'Acme Analytics' are not named in that file; the prompt asks to address ticket scenarios, not to cite ticket IDs or customer names in public docs.

TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md 'Common migration pitfalls' (line 185) lists sync, 202, hard delete, dataset.deleted and rate-limit pitfalls but not the API-key-deprecation pitfall from SUP-78234, which the agent had read. Each entry is a short note without symptoms or resolution steps, unlike its own escalated-ticket sections.

api_endpoints_data.csv gives version 2.1.0 for /auth/login, /auth/refresh, /auth/logout and /me/usage, but API_REFERENCE.md (GET /me/usage at line 645) records no version-added info, so these endpoints are not tied to v2.1.0 anywhere.
